Roadmap

Roadmap for **adjudicate** (CLI command `adj`; formerly the working name "dlog"): a Go, standard-library-only CLI that records project decisions as plain files in the repo. Owner decisions from 2026-10-15 are catalog records C23-C33.

Goals

adjudicate is a small CLI (`adj`) with a plain-text store that records project decisions as a loop: an agent asks, the owner decides in batches, and every later agent reads the decision. The goal and non-goal records below come from PROJECT.md; the owner's decisions on its open questions are catalog records C23-C33, and they override PROJECT.md where it differs (name, runtime, record format, license).

C01 Capture open questions in one command

Capture open questions with options and a recommendation in one command (PROJECT.md Goals 1).

C02 One inbox for batch answering

Show every open question in one inbox so the owner can answer them in a batch (Goals 2).

C03 Record decisions with rationale

Record a decision with a rationale and a link to the question it answers (Goals 3).

C04 Supersede with history

Supersede a decision while keeping its history (Goals 4).

C05 Compact agent context export

Export the accepted decisions as compact, token-cheap context, optionally filtered by tag or scope (Goals 5).

C06 Check before asking

Let an agent ask "has X been decided?" (check) before it asks the owner (Goals 6).

C07 Plain text in the repo

Store everything as plain text in the repo: diffable, mergeable, reviewable in a PR (Goals 7).

C08 Lint the log

Lint the log: missing fields, dangling links, supersede cycles, conflicting accepted decisions on the same key (Goals 8).

Non-goals

C09 No hosted service, database server, or web UI

v1 non-goal (PROJECT.md Non-goals).

C10 No LLM calls

adjudicate is a store and a workflow; agents bring their own reasoning (v1 non-goal).

C11 No cryptographic enforcement of who decided

v1 non-goal; owner-only decide is a convention in v1 (decision C27).

C12 Not a slicer replacement

Slicer tracks work; adjudicate tracks decisions. They link to each other by ID but neither depends on the other (v1 non-goal).

C13 No sync beyond git

No syncing across machines beyond what git already does (v1 non-goal).

Constraints

C33 Go caches and checks stay inside the repo

Owner constraint 2026-10-15. GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE and GOPATH point at a gitignored .cache/ under the repo root. No make: the env vars are documented in AGENTS.md and set by a small scripts/env.sh or an equivalent that the scaffolding slice (S02) decides. Tests run with go test ./... and go vet ./..., plus a gofmt check (gofmt -l lists no files).

Decisions

C23 Name: adjudicate, CLI command adj

Owner decision 2026-10-15. The tool is named adjudicate; the CLI command is `adj`; the Go module path is github.com/squalor-xyz/adjudicate. Replaces the working name 'dlog' (assumption C14, retired).

C24 Runtime: Go, standard library only

Owner decision 2026-10-15. Go (installed: go1.27.2 via Homebrew), standard library only, for runtime and tests (the `testing` package). Not Python. Any new dependency needs owner approval. Replaces assumption C15 (retired).

C25 Record format: Markdown body with JSON frontmatter

Owner decision 2026-10-15. One file per record: a Markdown body with JSON frontmatter, read and written with encoding/json. No TOML and no hand-written TOML parser or emitter. Owner's reason: the Go standard library has no TOML. The frontmatter delimiter is an implementer decision under the standing rule (C32). Replaces assumption C16 (retired).

C26 IDs: sequential, lint collision detection, renumber command

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). Sequential IDs: the next free ID comes from scanning the store; lint detects collisions; a renumber command resolves them. Which record keeps a colliding ID and the renumber command's name are implementer decisions under the standing rule (C32). Replaces assumption C17 (retired).

C27 Owner-only decide: convention in v1

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). Convention plus an AGENTS.md rule in v1: only the owner makes the decide transition. decided_by is recorded on each decision (attribution, not authentication); lint warns when it is missing. No git hook or signed commits in v1. Replaces assumption C18 (retired).

C28 Scope: per-repo in v1

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). v1 works on one repo's store; a cross-repo inbox is Later-tier work. Replaces assumption C19 (retired).

C29 Store: decisions/ at repo root, configurable

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). The store defaults to decisions/ at the repo root, and the config can change the path. Replaces assumption C20 (retired).

C30 Record kind: status alone, no kind field

Owner decision 2026-10-15. Records have no kind field; status alone carries it: open = a question; decided, rejected, withdrawn and superseded = answered. Replaces assumption C21 (retired).

C31 License: GPL-3.0-or-later

Owner decision 2026-10-15. The project is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Replaces assumption C22 (retired).

C32 Standing rule: implementer decides unfixed interface details

Owner decision 2026-10-15. Interface details not fixed by PROJECT.md or the owner's decisions are decided by the slice implementer: for example the config file name and format, how options and tradeoffs are passed on the CLI, how decided_by is supplied, check's match rule and exit codes, the context fields, whether lint warnings change the exit code, which record keeps a colliding ID, and the renumber command's name. The implementer records each such choice in the slicer catalog as a decision with a one-line reason; the reviewer checks it. The owner may overrule later.

C34 Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failed operation or check, 2 usage error

Matches slicer's exit codes (1 failed check, 2 usage or validation error), so agents read both tools the same way.

C35 CLI layout: cmd/adj calls internal/cli.Run with injected I/O

Run takes args, stdin, stdout and stderr and returns the exit code, so tests run the CLI in-process with buffers and main stays one line.

C36 Help flags: --help and -h print usage to stdout with exit 0; usage errors go to stderr with exit 2

Help is requested output on stdout; a missing or unknown command is an error, so its usage goes to stderr.

C37 env.sh extras: GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, GOFLAGS=-modcacherw, GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR under .cache/tmp

The workspace sandbox keeps Go inside the repo: no toolchain or module downloads, temp files under .cache/tmp, and -modcacherw lets the in-repo module cache be deleted without chmod.

C38 .gitignore: drop build/ and dist/, drop Python entries, add /adj, /bin/, *.test, *.out

No Python and no build/ or dist/ output: Check builds to .cache/bin/adj and a bare go build writes /adj, so both are ignored.

C40 env.sh: source from bash or zsh only; refuses to run unless the derived root has go.mod

Dash and other shells that are not bash or zsh cannot report the sourced path, and a wrong root would send caches and temp files outside the repo, so the script checks go.mod before it exports or creates anything.

C41 Record field types: dates as YYYY-MM-DD strings, integer ids, supersedes a list, superseded_by one id

A string in time.DateOnly form encodes as itself with encoding/json and keeps files deterministic. An old record is superseded by exactly one record, while a new record may replace several, so supersedes is []int and superseded_by is int (0 omitted).

C42 Required fields: id>0, title, status, created always; rationale and decided_at once answered; decision once decided or superseded; superseded_by once superseded

Rejected and withdrawn records need a why (PROJECT.md reject/withdraw --why) and a date but no decision text. decided_by is never required because lint warns instead (C27).

C43 History entry shape: {date, event, note}; event is the transition verb (ask, decide, reject, withdraw, supersede)

A flat list of three small fields stays readable in JSON frontmatter. Supersede puts 'by N' in note; creation (ask) is written by the code that creates the record, since model transitions start from open.

C44 Recommendation shape: {label, reasoning}, label must be one of the options

The table says the option label plus reasoning; two named fields keep the label machine-checkable and the reasoning free text.

C45 Transition API: Decide, Reject, Withdraw and Supersede mutate the record in place, take the date as a YYYY-MM-DD string, and leave the record untouched on error

Each builds and validates a copy before storing it, so a failed transition changes nothing, appends no history and never writes into the caller's slice. Errors match ErrInvalid; a status mismatch also matches ErrInvalidTransition.

C46 Supersede changes only the old record; setting the new record's supersedes link is the caller's job

The slice scopes a transition to one record and one history entry; linking the pair across two files belongs to the supersede command and store.

C47 Validate checks each history entry: a YYYY-MM-DD date and one of the five known events; blank decision and rationale text count as missing

A hand-edited file with a bad history date, an unknown event or whitespace-only why would otherwise load as valid; title already rejected blank text.

C48 Record fence: --- lines around the JSON frontmatter

The file opens with a --- line and the frontmatter ends at the first later line that is exactly ---; encoding/json writes no raw newline inside a string, so a fence cannot occur in the JSON, and body lines such as --- or } pass through intact. LF only: a file that starts with a byte order mark is rejected (file starts with a byte order mark), and so is a file whose frontmatter lines end in CR (CRLF line endings are not supported); both name the reason and match ErrInvalid. A closing fence at end of file with no newline is accepted, with an empty body.

C49 Markdown body is Record.Body with json:"-", kept verbatim

Each structured field lives once in the frontmatter and no field is repeated into the body, so the body is free Markdown that cannot drift from the fields.

C50 Marshal and Unmarshal both validate

Marshal refuses a record that Validate rejects and Unmarshal never returns an invalid record, so the strict read path cannot load a file the writer would not produce.

C51 Parse is the exported lenient decode with no Validate

Lint (S14) lives outside this package and must report invalid records rather than fail to load them; Unmarshal is Parse plus Validate.

C52 A non-empty body gets one final newline when it lacks one

Every file ends with a newline, so output is POSIX text and stable; a body that already ends in a newline is written byte for byte.

C53 Malformed and invalid files match ErrInvalid

Callers branch on one sentinel for every bad file, and the message still names the file.

C54 WriteFile uses os.WriteFile, not temp file and rename

Records are small text files; an atomic replace is left to the store slice if it needs one.

C55 ReadFile and WriteFile live in model/file.go, so model gains I/O

The slice Files list places them in model; they are the package's only file I/O, so AGENTS.md:23 and the record.go package doc change with them.

C56 Config: .adjudicate.json at the repo root, one JSON object with an optional store key

Unknown keys, an absolute store and a store that leaves the root are errors (invalid config); a missing file means the defaults (store decisions/). One standard-library format, and a typo in a key does not pass silently. The store-path check is lexical: a symlinked store can still point outside the root, and the config is owner-authored.

C57 Root discovery: nearest directory, from the working directory up, holding .adjudicate.json as a regular file

store.FindRoot returns it, or ErrNoRoot if none; adj init (later) writes the file. The config file is the one marker the owner already configures, and a directory of that name does not count. The walk goes to the file system root with no git boundary, so an .adjudicate.json in an ancestor directory applies.

C58 Record file name: <ID padded to four digits>-<slug>.md; slug is the title's lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by -, at most 60 bytes, untitled if empty

Non-ASCII characters and punctuation act as separators, so names are portable and diff-stable; 60 bytes keeps paths short; IDs above 9999 keep all digits.

C59 Record files are found by name: regular file, four or more digits above zero, then -, text and .md; the ID comes from the name

A file that does not parse still reserves its ID, so a broken file never lets Create reuse a number; List and Get reject a file whose record ID differs from its name.

C60 Duplicate IDs: List returns every file in ID then file-name order; Get and Update fail with ErrDuplicateID

Detecting and renumbering collisions is S15; the store must not silently pick one file, and Create still allocates one past the highest ID.

C61 List is strict: the first unreadable or invalid record file is an error naming it

Every command needs records that satisfy the model; lint (S14) uses model.Parse itself to report invalid files instead of loading them.

C62 Store writes go through a synced temp file: Update renames it over the record, Create links it into place and never replaces a file

Answers C54 for the store. The record is written to a .adj-*.tmp file (names start with a dot, so never taken for records) and fsynced. Update renames it over the record; after a crash the file is the old record or the new one, but the directory is not fsynced, so which one is not guaranteed. Create links it into place, so it can never overwrite a file; the link also keeps a reader from seeing half a record. Accepted limit: os.Link fails on file systems without hard links and there is no fallback. Concurrent creates in one checkout with different titles can still both get the same ID because the scan is not locked; lint (S14) detects that and renumber (S15) fixes it (C26).

C63 Create ignores the ID in the record and adds no history entry; the store directory is made on first Create; a missing directory is an empty store; Update keeps the file path

The ID is the store's to allocate (C26); the ask command writes the history entry and date (C43); an unrenamed file keeps git history and links to it.

C64 Permissions and retry: new records are 0644, Update keeps the old file's permission bits, and Create retries up to three times when its file name is taken

os.CreateTemp makes 0600 files, so the store sets the mode itself: 0644 for a new record (git-friendly, umask-independent) and the replaced file's bits on Update so a chosen mode survives. When the link finds the name taken (another writer after our scan), Create rescans and takes the next ID, then gives up with an error wrapping os.ErrExist that names the target file; no locking, which is the owner's design call.

C65 Root selection: --root DIR on every command, plus cli.Env.Root and Env.Stop; explicit roots are never searched

Tests run in temp dirs under the repo's own .cache, where walking up from the cwd could find the repo's real .adjudicate.json. --root DIR (flag wins) or the injected Env.Root names the root as it is: init uses it as is, other commands need DIR/.adjudicate.json in it. With neither, init uses the working directory and other commands search upward from it with store.FindRoot; Env.Stop bounds that walk (store.FindRootWithin, formerly the unexported findRoot) so a discovery test cannot leave its temp dir. --root is per command, not global, so it can sit among the other flags.

C66 Run keeps its signature; RunWith(Env, ...) takes clock, environment, working directory and root

C35 fixed Run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) for main; tests need a fixed clock, a fake environment and no use of the real cwd, so Run calls RunWith with the zero Env (real time.Now, os.Getenv, os.Getwd).

C67 Flags: one FlagSet per command; flags may follow positionals; -h/--help print the command usage to stdout (exit 0)

parseInterspersed splits arguments itself (a flag value is taken as the value even if it looks like a flag or is --) and then calls FlagSet.Parse once; a lone - and anything after -- are positional. Errors and usage go to stderr with exit 2, matching C36.

C68 adj ask --option LABEL:SUMMARY, tradeoffs as --tradeoffs LABEL:TEXT; both split at the first colon

A separate flag keeps the PROJECT.md --option shape and keeps colons in summaries unambiguous (a third colon field in --option would not). The label must name an option and each option takes one --tradeoffs; labels and texts are trimmed; blank labels are refused.

C69 adj ask recommendation reasoning: --reasoning TEXT, only with --recommend

The recommendation record has label and reasoning (C44); a flag next to --recommend is the smallest way to fill the second field, and reasoning with no recommendation is a usage error rather than silently dropped.

C70 asked_by: --by NAME, else the ADJ_ASKED_BY environment variable, else left blank

Agents set one environment variable once instead of repeating a flag; a blank is better than a guessed identity (C27 treats attribution as a convention). The flag wins so one command can override.

C71 adj ask context: --context TEXT, or --stdin to read it; both is a usage error; trailing newlines of stdin are trimmed

Long context is easier to pipe than to quote. Trimming only CR and LF at the end keeps leading indentation and inner blank lines, and the context field carries no stray final newline.

C72 adj init writes {"store": "decisions"} and creates the store directory; it acts on DIR or the cwd only, keeps an existing valid config, and prints initialized or already initialized

Spelling the one setting out shows the owner what to change (C56, C29). init never searches upward, so running it in a subdirectory starts a new root on purpose; a second run changes nothing, and an invalid or non-regular config fails with exit 1 before anything is created.

C73 Exit codes for init and ask: bad arguments exit 2 before any store access; no config (run adj init), an invalid config or a failed write exit 1

Follows C34: bad input is a usage error whatever the state of the store, and a missing store is a failed operation. ErrNoRoot is mapped to a message that says to run adj init.

C74 adj ask prints the new ID as a plain integer on stdout; created is the clock's local date

One machine-readable line (1, not 0001) is easy for agents to feed to later commands; the date is time.DateOnly of the injected clock, as C41 stores dates.

C75 adj ask tags: trimmed, blank is a usage error, repeats are dropped (first one kept, order kept)

An agent that repeats a tag meant the same tag, so de-duplicating is kinder than an exit 2; a blank tag is a typo and stays an error. --recommend is trimmed like option labels (C68).

C76 adj init removes the config it just wrote if creating the store directory fails; an existing config is never removed

A failed init must not leave a half-initialised repo, or ask would pass the config check and then fail; a config the owner wrote is theirs and stays.

C77 decided_by: --by NAME, else ADJ_DECIDED_BY, else blank

Reuses the C70 asked_by pattern for decide, reject and withdraw, so an agent sets one variable once; attribution only, not authentication (C27).

C78 decide takes an OPTION or --text, never both; OPTION is trimmed

Exactly one answer, as S07 states; the positional OPTION is trimmed like ask labels (C68), so " a " names option a.

C79 An OPTION the record does not offer is a usage error (exit 2)

Option labels live in the record, so this check runs after the record is read; unknown ID, not open and store failures stay exit 1 (C34).

C80 --why and --text are stored as typed; blank is a usage error

Matches --reasoning and --context (C69, C71), which keep their text; a blank reason or answer is refused before the store is read, as blank tags are (C75).

C81 decide, reject and withdraw print the record ID; the ID must be a positive integer

Same one-line output as adj ask (C74) so agents can chain commands; a non-number or 0 is a usage error (exit 2).

C82 Handlers: one file per command; UsageError moves to commands/errors.go

S06 review note: cli.go held every handler. init.go, ask.go and decide.go hold the handlers (decide.go has decide, reject and withdraw, which share flags and the store path); init and ask moved as is. Deviation from the Files list (cli.go, decide_test.go).

C83 An explicit empty --recommend is a usage error, as --tag "" is

S06 review note: --recommend "" was treated as absent; fsSet makes it exit 2 like a blank tag (C75).

C84 A record that is not open is refused before OPTION is checked

Refines C79 (S07 review): a decided record given an unknown OPTION exits 1 with the status error, because the status is the first thing the transition checks. Exit 2 is left for an OPTION the open record does not offer.

C85 A change to a record that is not open names its status and the change

Message: record N is S; only an open record can be V (V = decided, rejected or withdrawn), in place of the model text invalid record: transition not allowed. A notOpenError keeps the model error reachable through Unwrap, so errors.Is(err, model.ErrInvalidTransition) still holds.

C86 S08 list --json: one object with a records array

An object with a named key lets later fields such as counts be added without breaking readers, which a bare array would not; an empty store gives {"records": []}.

C87 S08 show --json: the record object, same shape as each list entry

One record shape for both commands so an agent parses one format; keys are the record file JSON names and empty keys are omitted, as in the file.

C88 S08 show prints the body and emits it as body

The body is the owner free Markdown, kept out of the frontmatter (C49) but still their text, so show prints it and JSON gives a body key only when it is non-empty.

C89 S08 list --tag repeats and every given tag must match

Mirrors the repeatable --tag of ask; a repeat narrows the result, consistent with the AND rule for combined filters.

C90 S08 list filters combine with AND

Each filter given must match, so every added flag narrows the result and no filter lists every record (slice proposal).

C91 S08 filter values: known status, no blank tag or key

Bad values exit 2 before the store is read (C73); a blank value is a typo, not no filter (C75, C83); --key matches the stored key as typed, since ask stores it untrimmed.

C92 S08 list order and empty results

List keeps store.List order (ID, then file name per C60); no match prints nothing in text and an empty records array in JSON with exit 0, because an empty answer is not a failure.

C93 S08 text layout for list and show

List prints one aligned line per record (ID, status, title) for grep; show prints a labelled line per set field so one field is easy to find, with multi-line values indented under their label.

C94 S08 show and list arguments

show takes one positive ID, and a bad ID is exit 2 as in decide (C81); list takes no positional arguments, since a stray word is a typo to report, not to ignore; an unknown or duplicate ID is exit 1 (C34).

C95 S08 handlers in cli/show.go and cli/list.go

C82 wants one handler file per command; the slice Files list omitted these two, so they are added and named in AGENTS.md Layout.

C96 S08 ask rejects a blank --key (exit 2)

ask stored a whitespace-only --key that list --key can never match (C91); like --tag it is now a usage error, while a real key is still stored as typed.

C97 S09 inbox arguments: adj inbox [--json] [--root DIR], no filters or positional arguments

The slice asks for open questions only; a stray word or a list filter is a usage error (exit 2) rather than silently ignored (C94), and adj list --status/--tag/--key already filter records.

C98 S09 inbox order: created date, then ID, ascending

Oldest question first answers the slice; created is a YYYY-MM-DD string so text order is date order (C41), and ID breaks ties and matches the store order. A sorted copy is made in commands, since store.List order is ID order (C92). The sort is stable, so equal records (same ID and date, C60) keep store.List order.

C99 S09 inbox --json: the list shape, {"records": [...]} of full record objects

Reuses render.RecordsJSON (C86, C87) so an agent parses one record shape; options with tradeoffs and the recommendation are already keys of the record. An empty inbox gives {"records": []}.

C100 S09 inbox text layout: 'ID title' then indented Created, Context, Options, Recommendation and Reasoning

The header keeps the ID and title greppable like list lines (C93); the owner needs when it was asked (the sort key), the options with summary and tradeoffs, and the asker's recommendation to answer in one batch. Context is shown too: owner decision 2026-10-15 (review of S09), multi-line context indented like other fields and omitted when empty. Key, tags and history are left to adj show.

C101 S09 empty inbox prints nothing in text and an empty array in JSON, exit 0

Same as an empty list (C92): an empty answer is not a failure, and a script can test for no output.

C102 S09 render trims trailing line breaks of option summaries, tradeoffs and history notes

S08 gate note: cont() indented the empty line after a trailing newline, printing a spaces-only line; these values now go through the same trim as other fields, and a value that is only line breaks counts as unset. writeField and writeOptions are shared by show and inbox.

C103 S09 handler files: cli/inbox.go, commands/inbox.go, render/inbox.go, plus commands/inbox_test.go and render/inbox_test.go

C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list names only cli/inbox_test.go; the oldest-first tie-break is only testable on unsorted input in package commands, and the text layout is tested in render beside the other golden tests.

C104 S09 docs/json.md inbox example is checked by a test

TestInboxJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample runs the CLI on a seeded repo and compares its output to the first json block of the inbox section, so the documented shape cannot drift from the real output.

C105 S10 check match rule: the trimmed query as a case-insensitive substring of title, key, any tag or the decision text

The slice proposal. The rationale is not searched: the slice names titles, keys, tags and decision text, and a rationale hit would report a record that is about something else. A blank query matches nothing (query.Search) and is a usage error in the CLI (C109).

C106 S10 check reports every status: decided and open as such, rejected, withdrawn and superseded in a closed list

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (S10 review), replacing the first rule that hid closed records. Search covers all statuses. A rejected, withdrawn or superseded match goes in the closed list, shown with its status (and superseded_by), so an agent sees that a topic was already closed and does not re-ask it. Closed records never count as decided.

C107 S10 check result precedence: decided, then open, then closed, then not found; both lists are always reported

Result is decided if the decided list is not empty (including the decided end of a supersede chain, C113), else open, else closed (a new result word), else not found. The decided record is what an agent must follow, so it wins; the other lists are still reported so an agent sees the follow-up question or the closed history. Exit codes do not depend on the result (C108).

C108 S10 check exit codes: 0 for every completed check (decided, open, closed and not found), 1 a failed check, 2 a usage error

The slice proposal, kept for agent scripts and confirmed by the owner in the S10 review: a non-zero exit means the check could not run (no repo, bad config, an unreadable record file), so a broken store is never mistaken for not found and then asked about. The answer is in the first line of the text or the result key of the JSON; C34's 1 and 2 are unchanged. Documented in the check usage, docs/json.md and AGENTS.md.

C109 S10 check arguments: exactly one QUERY; none, several or a blank one is a usage error (exit 2) before the store is read

A stray word is a typo to report (C94), and several words would need a rule for joining them, so the user quotes a query with spaces; the message says so. A blank query would match everything or nothing, so it is refused like a blank tag (C75, C91).

C110 S10 check output: first line is the result word; JSON is {query, result, decided, open, closed} with list-shaped records

Text: decided, open, closed or not found on line one, then ID status title per record (decided, open, then closed), with a decided record's Decision and Rationale and a superseded record's Superseded by indented under it. JSON: query (trimmed), result, and the decided, open and closed record arrays, always present and never null, so an agent reads one record shape (C86, C87). The result word is spelled the same in both: not found.

C111 S10 handler and render files: cli/check.go, commands/check.go, render/check.go, plus commands/check_test.go and render/check_test.go

C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list names only query/search.go, commands/check.go and cli/check_test.go; the text and JSON output is tested in render beside the other golden tests, and the blank-query rule in commands. render/json.go gained jsonRecords, shared with RecordsJSON.

C112 S10 docs/json.md check example is checked by a test

TestCheckJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample runs the CLI on a seeded repo and compares its output to the first json block of the check section, as C104 does for inbox, so the documented shape cannot drift from the real output.

C113 S10 check follows superseded_by from a superseded match to a decided record

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (S10 review). A superseded match stays in closed; its superseded_by is followed through superseded records, bounded by visiting each record once, to the end of the chain. If the end is a decided record it is added to decided (once, in ID order, even if it also matched). A chain that stops at a missing ID, at a record that is neither superseded nor decided, or in a repeat (a loop) adds nothing. This way an agent that finds a replaced decision is led to the decision in force.

C114 ID allocation is locked with flock

Owner decision 2026-10-15: store.Create holds an advisory flock (unix) across the ID scan and the link, so concurrent asks in one checkout cannot share an ID. Branch/clone collisions stay with lint/renumber (S14/S15). Implemented in S23, after S15.

C115 S11 context selects status decided only, in ID order

The slice says only decided appears; superseded records are left out because their replacement is decided (C113 leads check the same way). Order is store.List order (ID, C92), so the same store gives the same bytes.

C116 S11 context entry fields: id, title, key, decision, first line of the rationale

The slice proposal: enough to follow a decision (what and why in one line) without options, context, tags or history; adj show has the rest. key is left out when unset, as in a record (C87).

C117 S11 context rationale is the first non-blank line, trimmed

A rationale is free text that may run to paragraphs; the first line keeps entries compact (Risks: context bloat). Leading blank lines are skipped so a rationale that starts with a line break still shows a reason. The decision text is kept whole, since it is the answer.

C118 S11 context --format md|json, default md, exact lowercase; any other value is a usage error

The slice proposal; md is the form an agent reads or pastes. Checked before the store is read (C73), like a bad status (C91); an explicit empty value is refused too (C83), not read as the default.

C119 S11 context md layout: a list entry '- ID title [key]: decision' then ' Rationale: first line'; no header; empty prints nothing

Compact and diff-stable: one list line per decision with the key in brackets (omitted when unset), the rationale indented under it, a multi-line decision continuing on lines indented four spaces. No header, so an empty result is no output (C101) and the caller adds its own framing. Reuses writeField and cont from text.go.

C120 S11 context --format json: {"decisions": [{id, title, key?, decision, rationale?}]}, empty is an empty array

An object with a named key lets fields be added later (C86); the key is decisions, not records, because an entry is not the full record object. docs/json.md has the shape and TestContextJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample checks the example against real output (C104).

C121 S11 context --tag repeats, every tag must match, trimmed; --key-prefix is a plain string prefix of the stored key as typed; blank values are usage errors

Reuses list's rules (C89, C91): AND semantics, trimmed tags, key matched as typed. The prefix is not dot-aware (storage also matches storagex) because the slice names a key prefix and a plain prefix is the least surprising; a record with no key never matches. query.Filter gains KeyPrefix.

C122 S11 context takes no positional arguments; flags may come before or after; --json is not a context flag

A stray word is a typo to report (C94, C97). The format flag is --format as the slice names it, so list's --json does not carry over.

C123 S11 handler files: cli/context.go, commands/context.go, render/context.go, plus query/filter_test.go and render/testdata/context.md, context.json

C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list omits query (Filter.KeyPrefix and its test). The golden files in render/testdata are shared: render tests build the four records by hand and cli tests read the same files through a seeded store.

C124 S12 adj ai prints the embedded snippet internal/commands/ai.md and takes no flag or argument, not even --root

It reads no repo, so --root would do nothing; a stray argument is a typo to report, as for inbox and context (C94, C97, C122). Markdown file via embed so the snippet reads as it will be pasted.

C125 S12 the snippet is tested against the CLI: every adj command it names has --help, every flag in an adj code span is a whole word in that command's usage, every ADJ_ variable is in a usage, at most 1800 bytes

The snippet is pasted into other repos' AGENTS.md and cannot be checked there, so a rename or removed flag must fail here; the size cap keeps it token-cheap (Risks: adoption). Whole-word matching so --reason does not pass for --reasoning.

C126 S12 the snippet tells agents to check, read (context, show), ask and withdraw their own question, and never to run adj decide or adj reject

Owner confirmed 2026-10-15: agents may withdraw their own questions (never another agent's or the owner's; C130). C27 makes only the decide transition the owner's; withdraw is the asker's own close and records no decision, so an agent can drop a stale question. adj supersede is not named until S13 adds it.

C127 S12 json shape test: docs/json.md first json block under each command heading is the shape; show and list are pinned by a fixture that matches their examples byte for byte; record keys must be in the Keys of a record table, which must equal model.Record json tags plus body

Record keys are omitted when empty (C87), so a key list taken from output would vary; a byte-exact fixture pins show and list, the table is pinned to the model by reflection, and context entries are checked against their own table. docsJSONExample and jsonBlockUnder moved to jsonshape_test.go so one convention reads the docs (S09 review, C104).

C128 S12 withdraw usage describes --by as who withdrew it; docs/json.md context rationale row says the first non-blank line

S07 gate nit: who decided reads oddly for a withdrawal (reject keeps who decided); S11 gate nit: code, C117 and AGENTS.md already say first non-blank line, the docs table said first line.

C129 S12 snippet flag drift check: a flag in any code span is checked against the nearest preceding adj CMD span

Review LOW: prose spans such as 'or pass --by NAME' were not covered; attributing by position keeps the prose natural without moving every flag into an adj span.

C130 S12 snippet limits: withdraw only your own question and with --by NAME (ADJ_DECIDED_BY is the owner's and not named); on closed read adj show ID and never re-ask a rejected question; on no repo tell the owner, do not run adj init

Review MEDIUM/LOW: withdraw records decided_by, so an agent names itself with --by; a rejected question was decided against, so re-asking it wastes the owner's batch; init is the owner's setup step. Refines C126.

C131 LICENSE is the full GPL-3.0 text; NOTICE holds the Squalor LLC copyright

Owner decision 2026-10-15: copyright holder is Squalor LLC. LICENSE is the verbatim GPL-3.0 text supplied by the owner (the license forbids changing it), so the copyright line and the or-later notice live in NOTICE.

C132 check text shows the rationale under closed records

Owner decision 2026-10-15: adj check text prints the rationale under rejected, withdrawn and superseded matches, so an agent sees why a topic was closed. Implemented in S24.

C133 S13 adj supersede OLD --by NEW [--root DIR]: --by is the replacing record's ID, there is no --why and no who flag

The slice names OLD --by NEW. --by here is an ID, not an author as in decide, so the owner's name is not recorded: model.Supersede takes no rationale or actor and the old record keeps its own rationale. Extra arguments, a missing --by, and a --by that is not a positive integer are usage errors (exit 2).

C134 S13 supersede prints OLD's ID and exits 0; OLD equal to NEW is a usage error (2); unknown ID or a record that is not decided is exit 1, OLD checked first

Like decide, reject and withdraw it prints the ID of the record it changed (C74). Equal IDs are bad input that needs no record, so they exit 2 before the store is looked for (C73); a missing or not-decided record is a failed operation (C34), and the message names the status, as decide's does.

C135 S13 model.LinkSupersedes(r, old, date) is the new record's half of a supersede: adds old to supersedes once, appends one supersede history entry with note 'supersedes N'

C46 leaves the new record's link to the caller; apply is unexported, so a model function keeps the same validate-a-copy, record-untouched-on-error guarantee (C45) instead of duplicating it in the command. The history event is supersede, the five events of C43 stay unchanged, and the note mirrors 'by N' on the old record. The slice allows extending transition.go only if needed; this is why.

C136 S13 supersede validates both records in memory, writes OLD first, and if NEW then fails puts OLD back; if that fails too the error says the store is inconsistent

Two files cannot be written atomically (C62 is per file). OLD first because the worst leftover, OLD superseded and NEW decided without its link back, still leaves one decision in force (check and context agree); NEW first could leave two decided records that contradict each other. The restore makes the common failure leave both records unchanged; the error names the leftover state when it cannot.

C137 S13 the agent snippet's never-run list gains adj supersede

Superseding changes a decision, so it is owner-only like decide and reject (C27, C126). The S12 gate note asked for it; ai_test checks the list names it, as the drift test only checks that named commands exist.

C39 LICENSE is a stub until the owner supplies the full GPL-3.0 text and copyright holder

No GPL-3.0 text exists in the adjudicate repo and the workspace has no network, so the stub carries the SPDX line, the or-later notice and TODO(owner) markers.

Retired: Replaced by the full GPL-3.0 text and NOTICE (owner supplied the text and named Squalor LLC, 2026-10-15).. Successor: C131.
